timeout_ms.description: Startup timeout in milliseconds. Values must be greater than 3000 and at most 300000.

PaneCarveClearParams.description:
fork(+131): release a carve and let the pane re-expand. Same asymmetry as
the other clear methods: a plugin releases only its own, while a socket
caller (`owner` empty) releases the pane outright, because the user at the
CLI outranks any plugin — and this is the manual escape hatch if a carve
ever outlives its owner.

PaneCarveEdge.description:
fork(+131): which edge of a pane a carve reserves.

A carve is not an overlay and cannot borrow the overlay's free placement. A
PTY is a RECTANGLE: `resize` takes a row count and a column count and
nothing else, so the only regions a terminal can be made to stop using are
full-width bands at the top or bottom and full-height columns at the left or
right. There is no way to carve a hole in the middle — the terminal has no
concept of one.

Hence a distinct type rather than reusing `PaneGraphicsPlacementParams`.
Accepting a free `viewport_col`/`grid_cols` placement here would accept
placements the host cannot honour and then quietly do something else, which
is the failure this API family has now been bitten by twice (#33's silently
defaulted field names, #40's `0`-means-whole-pane).

PaneCarveSetParams.description:
fork(+131): reserve part of a pane so the TERMINAL stops using it.

Unlike `pane.graphics.set`/`pane.text.set`, this is not a compositing call.
It resizes the PTY, so the program in the pane reflows and its scrollback is
rewritten — ordinary resize behaviour that shells and agents already handle
(the user causes it constantly with splits and zooms), but a real side
effect rather than a per-frame paint. That is the difference +127 deferred:
not that reflow is hazardous, but that doing it ACCIDENTALLY is.

Identity is `(owner, pane_id)` — one carve per owner per pane, replaced on
repeat rather than accumulated, because a plugin asking twice means "this is
my band now", not "give me two". Cleanup on owner loss is mandatory and
lives host-side: a plugin gets no unload event, and a dead plugin must never
leave a pane permanently shrunk.

cells.description: Thickness in CELLS: rows for a top/bottom band, columns for left/right.

layer_id.description:
fork(+127): which of the owner's layers to clear. Omitted (the default)
clears ALL layers this caller owns on the pane, which is exactly the
pre-+127 behaviour — so an existing caller that never learned about
`layer_id` still wipes what it painted. Naming one clears only that layer.

Ignored for the privileged socket caller (`owner == None`), which clears
the whole pane regardless; see `handle_pane_graphics_clear`.

PaneGraphicsPlacement.description:
Where a pane-graphics (or pane-text) layer sits, in terminal CELLS.

# Why this lives HERE and not in the host

It used to live only in the herdr binary crate, as
`api::schema::PaneGraphicsPlacementParams`. Guests cannot reach that, so
every guest hand-rolled the JSON object — and got no compile-time check on
the field names. `claude-image-preview` shipped `col`/`row` instead of
`viewport_col`/`viewport_row` for its entire life: the host accepted the
call, discarded the unknown keys, defaulted the real fields, and painted
every image at the pane's top-left, stacked over the text it was annotating.
The call returned success and logged nothing, and the plugin's own test
suite was green because it asserted on the same wrong names.

Sharing the type is the only fix that makes that class of mistake a COMPILE
error rather than a silent misrender. `deny_unknown_fields` on the host
makes it a loud runtime error for callers that still build JSON by hand;
this makes it impossible for callers that do not.

# Extents are `Option`, and `Some(0)` is invalid

A missing extent means "the whole pane in that axis" — the long-standing
default, and the reason `Default` is still meaningful. An extent that is
present but zero is REJECTED rather than silently meaning whole-pane,
because those two are worlds apart on screen and the difference used to be
one typo wide: any misspelled key defaulted its real field to 0, and 0 read
as "fill the pane", so a typo became a full-pane opaque overlay.

grid_cols.description: Width in cells. `None` = the full pane width. `Some(0)` is an error.

grid_rows.description: Height in cells. `None` = the full pane height. `Some(0)` is an error.

viewport_col.description:
Column of the layer's left edge, relative to the pane's text viewport.
May be negative: a placement starting off the left edge paints its
visible remainder, matching kitty.

viewport_row.description: Row of the layer's top edge. Negative is legal, as above.

layer_id.description:
fork(+127): identifies this layer WITHIN its owner, so one caller can hold
several coexisting layers on one pane.

Before +127 a layer's identity was its owner alone: one layer per plugin
per pane, and a second `set` replaced the first. That is fine for a single
panel image and impossible for the Claude `[Image #N]` case, where one
plugin must paint every placeholder visible in a pane at once.

Identity is the pair `(owner, layer_id)`. Empty (the default) is a real
id, not "unset" — it is the one every pre-+127 caller uses, which is why
their single-layer behaviour is unchanged.

source_path.description:
fork: absolute path to an image file the HOST reads instead of taking
bytes over the wire. Empty (the default) keeps the original `data_base64`
behaviour.

Exists because the two callers have asymmetric power. A socket caller can
already open the file itself and base64 it, so for that caller this is
only an efficiency win and stays unrestricted. A UI-plugin caller cannot:
the wasm guest has no WASI and no imports. For that caller the path must
resolve, after canonicalisation, under one of the roots its manifest
declared in `graphics_roots` — otherwise `source_path` would hand a
sandboxed guest an arbitrary-file-read primitive.

It also sidesteps the 512 KiB `data_base64` cap, which exists only
because that payload rides a single JSON line on the socket. A file read
has no such constraint and is capped at the streaming limit instead.

PaneTextClearParams.description:
fork(+128): drop text overlays. Mirrors `PaneGraphicsClearParams` exactly,
including the asymmetry: a plugin clears only what it owns, while a socket
caller (`owner` empty) clears the pane outright, because the user at the CLI
outranks any plugin.

PaneTextLineParams.description: fork(+128): one row of an overlay, as a sequence of styled spans.

PaneTextSetParams.description:
fork(+128): retain a TEXT overlay on a pane.

The deliberate non-goal, and the reason this is not `pane.write` or an edit
API: it does not mutate the terminal. The lines are composited into the
ratatui buffer for the frame, exactly like a `pane.graphics` layer, and
`PaneState`/scrollback never see them. Search, copy, resume and agent
detection keep reading the real program output, so a plugin cannot corrupt
what an agent believes it printed — the property `.local/prd/127-plugin-owned-images.md`
reserved for this stage.

Identity, placement and cleanup are intentionally the same model as
`PaneGraphicsSetParams`: `(owner, layer_id)`, cell-grid placement relative to
the pane's inner rect, and removal when the owning plugin goes away. A plugin
author who has learned one has learned the other.

PaneTextSpanParams.description:
fork(+128): one styled run within an overlay line.

Colours are NAMED, never RGB. Herdr renders buffer colours through the
active theme palette, and a truecolor `Rgb` passes through it untouched —
so an overlay that picked its own hex would be the one
element on screen that ignores the user's theme, and would do it silently.
An unrecognised name is treated as "unset" rather than refused: a plugin
naming a colour the host does not know should lose the styling, not the text.

bg.description:
Named background, same vocabulary as `fg`. Empty keeps the cell's own
background, which is what makes a span composite over pane text rather
than punching a hole in it.

fg.description:
Named foreground: `black`, `red`, `green`, `yellow`, `blue`, `magenta`,
`cyan`, `gray`/`grey`, `white`, each also available as `bright_*`. Empty
(the default) inherits whatever the cell already had.

PluginUiStatusParams.description:
fork(+127): params for `plugin.ui.status`. Both filters are optional; omitting
both returns every registered UI module.

oneOf.description: Outer popup size in terminal cells, including the border.
Outer popup size as a percentage of the terminal area, for example 80%.

ResumePickerOpenParams.description:
Open the resume-search picker as an in-app overlay. `wrapper` is the
absolute path to `resume-picker-overlay.sh` (the caller — the button script —
resolves it from `$HERDR_PLUGIN_ROOT`, keeping plugin layout out of the host).

hidden.description:
Create the tab already hidden.

A hidden tab exists, runs, and is reachable through `tab.list
{hidden:true}` — it is simply not drawn in the tab bar or the sidebar.
Contradictory with `focus`, and rejected rather than silently resolved:
there is no sensible answer to "focus the tab you cannot see".
When set, restrict the result to tabs with this visibility state.

focus.description: Reveal the tab and focus it when true. Defaults to false.

oneOf.description:
fork(+128): the text-overlay half of the pane-compositing API. Kept
beside the graphics methods rather than under `pane.write` or an edit
namespace because it composites at render time and never mutates the
terminal — same lifetime, same identity, same capability.

fork(+131): carve — reserve an edge band so the TERMINAL stops using it.
Beside the compositing methods because it serves the same feature, but a
distinct pair because it is a distinct ACT: these two resize the PTY.

warnings.description:
Warnings collected at link time or on registry load (e.g. unknown event names,
missing manifest file). Non-fatal — the entry is kept and surfaced by plugin.list.

PluginHostActionMode.description: fork(host-actions): schema mirror of the host's `HostActionMode`.

oneOf.description: The host runs its default body and the module is also told.
The host skips its default body; the module owns the outcome.

collector.description:
fork(wave-2): optional argv naming a command the host executes on each
dashboard tick to PRODUCE this module's snapshot out-of-process, so
collection logic hot-reloads (rebuild the bin) without a host rebuild.
Relative `argv[0]` is resolved against `plugin_root` at exec time. The
host gates and spawns it exactly like a plugin `event`/`action` command
(same executor path); the child receives `HERDR_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR` and
`HERDR_FOCUS_JSON`, and answers on stdout with the sticky snapshot
protocol (`{"outcome":"replace","snapshot":{…}}` | `{"outcome":"keep"}`
| `{"outcome":"clear"}`). Only meaningful together with `ui_input_file`.

graphics_roots.description:
fork: absolute directory roots this module may load images from at
runtime via `pane.graphics.set { source_path }`. Only meaningful together
with the `pane_graphics` capability.

This is the dynamic generalisation of `image_file` above. `image_file` is
fixed at manifest time, which cannot serve an image whose path is chosen
per frame (a Claude session's `<session>/<N>.png`, say). `source_path`
can — so the roots it may reach have to be declared up front rather than
chosen by the guest, and they are visible in the manifest and in
`plugin list` before anyone enables the plugin.

Empty (the default) means a plugin-owned `set` may not use `source_path`
at all. This is the whole security story of the field: a wasm guest has
no WASI and no host imports, so it cannot read a file — `source_path` is
the only way it can cause the host to read one on its behalf, and an
undeclared root makes that a refusal rather than a filesystem oracle.

host_action_mode.description:
fork(host-actions): whether claiming a control suppresses the host's own
behaviour. Omitted means [`PluginHostActionMode::Observe`] — a manifest
that names a control without saying more gets the events and changes
nothing the user can see.

host_actions.description:
fork(host-actions): stable `host.*` ids of host-drawn controls this
module wants. An id the host does not define fails the manifest LOAD
rather than being dropped later — a claim that cannot resolve to a real
control would otherwise sit in `plugin list` looking live while doing
nothing, which is the silent-failure mode this lane exists to prevent.

Only honoured together with the `host_actions` capability.

image_file.description:
fork: optional single path segment naming an image file under this
module's plugin directory. When declared, the HOST loads it and paints
it over the module's surface `Rect` (kitty transmit path, or half-block
fallback). Purely host-consumed — it never crosses the wasm guest ABI.

max_layers_per_pane.description:
fork(+127): ceiling on how many `pane.graphics` layers this plugin may
hold on ONE pane. Omitted means the host default (8); the host clamps any
value to a hard maximum (32).

Declared rather than implicit because +127 changed layer identity from
`owner` to `(owner, layer_id)`, which is what lets one plugin paint many
images at once — and each retained layer holds its bytes in host memory
for as long as it exists. A declared ceiling is visible in `plugin list`
before anyone enables the plugin and makes the worst-case footprint of
enabling it something you can read off the manifest instead of measure.

placement.description:
Data-driven placement for this module's `Panel` surface. Only consulted
when the module declares the `panel` surface; ignored otherwise. `None`
falls back to the `PluginPanelPlacement` default (free overlay).

rail_icon.description:
Glyph the host paints for this module in the right-panel rail.

The rail glyph used to come from a hardcoded table of `builtin.` plugin
ids in `src/ui.rs`, so every third-party right-panel plugin got the same
generic marker and could only be told apart by clicking it. The icon is
the plugin's own identity, so it belongs in the plugin's own manifest.
One or two display cells of non-control text; omitted keeps the fallback.

ui_input_file.description:
Optional single path segment (no separators, no `..`) naming a file under
this module's `HERDR_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR`. When declared, the host reads the
file each frame (size-capped, mtime-cached) and injects its contents as
`HERDR_PLUGIN_UI_INPUT_JSON` in the module's frame env (spec §7.1). The
plugin's own process side writes the file; the host never interprets it.

PluginPanelPlacement.description:
Data-driven placement for a `Panel` surface (schema mirror of the host's
generic panel layout). Every field is manifest DATA, so a plugin controls
where it renders with no host/enum change. Defaults reproduce a free overlay
with a snug (content-sized) box.

align.description:
Where the panel sits along the carve axis of its region. Meaningful for
`bottom_band` (which side of the usage band) and `free` (anchor within
the pane area); edge regions (`left`/`right`/`top`/`bottom`) already
encode their edge.

min_peer.description:
Cells (columns for vertical bands, rows for horizontal bands) the peer
region keeps: the panel is only carved when the peer keeps at least this
much, so a secondary panel never squeezes the primary content unreadable.

region.description: Which region the panel occupies / carves from.

size.description:
Extent along the carved dimension: `"auto"` (snug to content, default),
a cell count (`"30"`), or a percent of the available span (`"30%"`).
Parsed host-side; unparseable values fall back to `auto`.

z.description: Draw/hit z-order among panels and other layers (higher is on top).

oneOf.description:
Share the usage-strip band: carve a slot beside the usage dash (its own
rect + hit-rects). This is what button-dash uses.
Carve a column band from the left/right of the pane area (panes shrink).
Carve a row band from the top/bottom of the pane area (panes shrink).
Overlay the pane area without carving; anchored by `align`.
API v3 (§5.3): read-only socket API methods via `HostEffect::Api`.
API v3 (§5.3): structural write socket API methods via `HostEffect::Api`.

API v3 (§5.3): text/keystroke-injecting socket API methods via
`HostEffect::Api` (`pane.send_text`, `agent.send_keys`).

fork: `pane.graphics.*` via `HostEffect::Api` — painting an image into a
pane's cell grid. Deliberately NOT folded into `ApiWrite`: drawing over a
pane is a different power from splitting or closing one, it is the only
capability that puts pixels on screen outside the plugin's own surface,
and separating it means `plugin list` shows exactly which plugin holds
the right to draw into the user's panes.

fork(host-actions): observe or replace the host-drawn controls named in
`host_actions`. Kept out of `MouseAll` because that one only lets a
module SEE clicks, while this one lets it suppress a native button —
a different power, so a separate, refusable, `plugin list`-visible grant.

fork(host-actions): exclusive keyboard routing while a plugin modal is
open (`HostEffect::SetKeyboardCapture`). Separate from `keyboard_input`
(a broadcast copy) because capture REDIRECTS keys away from the pane —
a strictly larger power that must be its own visible grant.

fork: `plugin.enable`/`plugin.disable` via `HostEffect::Api`. Kept out of
`ApiWrite` for the same reason as the two above: a module holding this
can switch OTHER modules off, so it has to be declared and visible in
`plugin list` rather than arriving as a side effect of ordinary writes.
`plugin.link`/`plugin.unlink` remain host-reserved — installing code from
a path is a strictly larger power than flipping an installed plugin's
enabled bit, and nothing in-guest needs it.

PluginUiModuleStatus.description:
fork(+127): read-only live status of one registered UI module.

This type is the answer to the question that cost hours: *what is actually
loaded in this running instance, and if my thing is not showing, why not?*
Before it, answering that required rebuilding a mirror sandbox of the whole
config, because nothing on the wire distinguished "module failed to load"
from "module loaded and produced nothing" from "module produced nodes that
did not fit". Each of those is a different field here.

Strictly read-only and side-effect free, so it is safe to poll and safe to
expose to plugins themselves under `api_read`.

capabilities.description:
Capabilities the manifest requested. Shown so "my API call is being
denied" can be checked against what was actually granted without reading
the manifest off disk.

collector_declared.description: Whether this module declares an out-of-process collector.

enabled.description:
Whether the owning plugin is enabled in the registry. A module can be
registered-but-disabled; distinguishing that from "not registered" is the
first fork in the diagnostic tree.

hit_rects.description:
Declared `UiHitRect` count in the current layers. Zero on a module whose
clicks "do nothing" means the module never published a target; non-zero
moves the investigation to coordinates.

last_error.description:
Last load / hot-reload / guest-call error, or `None` if the last attempt
succeeded.

last_skip_reason.description:
fork(+127): why this module's PANEL was dropped in the last laid-out
frame, if it was. `None` means it was not dropped — either it rendered or
it declares no panel surface.

layer_count.description:
How many `pane.graphics` layers this module's PLUGIN currently holds,
across every pane, and how many bytes they retain.

Plugin-scoped, not module-scoped, because layer ownership is stamped with
the plugin id — that is also the granularity `plugin disable` operates at.
`layer_bytes` is the honest per-plugin RAM number for graphics: guest
memory lives inside a wasm instance and is invisible to `footprint`, so
the host accounting here is the only way to attribute it.

loaded.description:
Whether a guest instance is live right now. `false` with `last_error` set
is a load/hot-reload failure; `false` with no error means never loaded.

negotiated_version.description:
The version actually negotiated with the guest's export. A mismatch with
`api_version_declared` is silent at runtime and changes which events the
module receives, which makes it worth showing side by side.

panel_content_w.description:
Content dims measured for the panel in the last laid-out frame. `(0, 0)`
with `last_skip_reason == "no_content"` is the "module produced nothing"
case; non-zero dims with a skip reason is the "did not fit" case.

rendered_content_w.description:
Measured content dims of the module's panel layers this frame,
independent of whether the panel was skipped.

rendered_surfaces.description:
Whether this module produced any layer in the frame most recently laid
out, and how much it produced.

`panel_content_w/h` above are populated from the panel SKIP record, so a
module that renders perfectly reports 0x0 there — read together with a
`layer_count` that only covers pane layers, a healthy painting module was
indistinguishable from a dead one. Four wrong diagnoses of the right rail
survived on exactly that ambiguity. These fields answer the question
directly: what did this module paint, and where.

wasm_memory_bytes.description:
Linear memory held by the loaded guest instance, invisible to the process
footprint. `None` when the module is not loaded.

oneOf.description: The multi-row usage dashboard strip (host `usage_strip_rect`). API v2.

A generic, plugin-placed panel whose rect the host lays out from the
module manifest `placement` spec (region/align/size/min_peer/z) rather
than a hardcoded per-variant match. Adding/moving/resizing a panel is a
pure manifest edit (hot-reload), no host rebuild.
Outer popup size in terminal cells, including the border.
Outer popup size as a percentage of the terminal area, for example 80%.

cols.description:
fork(+130): the pane's CELL extents — its inner rect, chrome
excluded, which is the rect placements are resolved against.

`cell_*_px` alone was never enough to place anything: it says how big
one cell is, not how many cells there are, so a caller could compute
an image's pixel size and still had no idea whether it would fit or
where the right edge was. That is why `image-view` and
`claude-image-preview` both ended up with refit logic nothing could
drive.

`None` when the pane is not currently laid out — a pane in a
background tab has no rect this frame. Deliberately `Option` rather
than `0`: `0` is the value the placement API overloads to mean "the
whole pane" (#40), so reporting it for an unknown extent would tell a
caller the exact opposite of the truth.

oneOf.description: fork(+127): see `PluginUiModuleStatus`.
